Senses relating to physical conflict:
To engage in combat with; to oppose physically, to contest with.

examples.text: My grandfather fought the Nazis in World War II.

glosses: Senses relating to physical conflict:
To conduct or engage in (battle, warfare, a cause, etc.).

examples.text: Our soldiers fought the battle just over that hill.
I have fought a good fight.
Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
was left to fight his way through the world.

glosses: Senses relating to physical conflict:
To contend in physical conflict, either singly or in war, battle etc.

examples.text: A wounded animal will fight tooth and nail; relentless, savage and murderous.

glosses: Senses relating to physical conflict:
To contend in physical conflict with each other, either singly or in war, battle etc.

examples.text: The two boxers have been fighting for more than half an hour.

glosses: Senses relating to physical conflict:
To cause to fight; to manage or manoeuvre in a fight.

examples.text:
And so we made their grave where they should lie
Close side by side, as they had fought their tank
Through every fight, arm touching arm.
We made it deep, that nothing of the conflict they had left above
Should break into their peace.
to fight cocks; to fight one’s ship

glosses: To strive for something; to campaign or contend for success.

examples.text: He fought for the Democrats in the last election.

glosses: To try to overpower; to fiercely counteract.

examples.text: The government pledged to fight corruption.

examples.text: One of them got stuck in a chokehold and got stabbed to death during the fight.

glosses: A battle between opposing armies.

examples.text: Watch your language! Are you looking for a fight?

glosses: A boxing or martial arts match.

examples.text: I’m going to Nick’s to watch the big fight tomorrow night.
